clue.text: Dashes round in varieties of colour

definitions.note: plural noun phrase matching the plural answer

indicators.note: turning the letters round suggests they are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone darts about among a range of paint colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a description of the dashing, but it signals an anagram of DASHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are tints or tones, the gradations of a hue.

clue.text: Complaint of a, painstaking Principal

parts.note: a school head who takes pains has pain in the head, the ailment read from its two parts

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a conscientious head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the head, the ailment of a head teacher taking pains.

clue.text: Politicians with catlike qualities?

parts.note: cats are said to have nine lives, so they are hard to kill, like politicians who resist all change

explanation.surface: MPs who behave like felines.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn conservatives who resist reform to the last, as a cat survives with nine lives.

clue.text: Aside, in a matter of speaking

definitions.meaning: an aside is a remark made quietly so others do not hear
a play on 'in a manner of speaking', describing a way of using the voice

explanation.surface: A parenthetical remark, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian phrase means 'under the voice', in an undertone.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'under the voice': spoken quietly, as in a stage murmur.

clue.text: Take steps to win without trying

definitions.text: Take steps to win without trying

parts.words: Take steps to win without trying
parts.note: an easy victory where one need only stroll across the line, the literal stepping over and the sporting sense of an uncontested win

explanation.surface: Advice on how to triumph with no effort at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory granted when no opponent turns up, so the winner merely has to stroll the course.

clue.text: Bill showing fruit half a-crown?

parts.note: a Bill named with a citrus fruit who held half of a joint throne, sharing it with his wife Mary

explanation.surface: An invoice listing fruit priced at an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Half a crown was an old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence; here it means half of a shared monarchy, as William III reigned jointly with Mary II.
explanation.definitionFit: William III, Prince of Orange, shared the English crown with Mary II.

clue.text: Rings for attendants

definitions.meaning: guard rings worn to keep another ring from slipping off
custodians or wardens who look after something

explanation.surface: Bells ring to summon the servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Guard rings that hold another ring on a finger, and people who tend a zoo or museum.

clue.text: Its inhabitants are a waspish lot

definitions.text: Its inhabitants are a waspish lot

parts.words: Its inhabitants are a waspish lot
parts.note: waspish literally, a dwelling occupied by stinging insects rather than ill-tempered people

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood full of irritable residents.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest of wasps, from the Latin vespa.

clue.text: Ten girls arranged their coiffure

definitions.note: plural curls making up a hairdo, matching the plural answer

indicators.note: arranging the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Ten girls have their hair done.
explanation.definitionFit: Long curls of hair, the style the girls wear.

clue.text: Like the responsibility of Dad taking on a hire charge

indicators.note: Dad is followed by, taking on, the hire charge as the next part

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
a rental is the fee charged for hiring something

explanation.surface: A father who has to pay a hire fee as part of his duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes what belongs to a mother or father, as in 'parental responsibility'.

clue.text: Summer wear in school ?

parts.note: in hot weather one wears ..., and split differently that phrase is also something taught in a school

explanation.surface: A question about the uniform pupils wear in hot months.
explanation.definitionFit: A class or period of teaching, the unit of instruction in a school.

clue.text: A dandy, or maniac perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether a flamboyant man is a fop or simply mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OR MANIAC. An 18th-century macaroni was a fashionable young man affecting continental dress.
explanation.definitionFit: In 18th-century Britain a macaroni was a foppish dresser who copied Italian fashions.

clue.text: A word of no significance

parts.note: read literally, a statement whose meaning is simply 'no', a refusal or contradiction

explanation.surface: A remark that means nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or contradiction, saying that something is not so.

clue.text: They are passed over in and out

definitions.text: They are passed over in and out

parts.words: They are passed over in and out
parts.note: mats at a threshold are walked across by everyone entering and leaving, and meek people are also passed over

explanation.surface: People repeatedly overlooked at every turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mats laid at entrances for wiping shoes, also a term for people who let others walk all over them.

clue.text: Flimnap held this office in Lilliput

definitions.text: Flimnap held this office in Lilliput

parts.words: Flimnap held this office in Lilliput
parts.note: in Gulliver's Travels Flimnap is the Lilliputian minister in charge of the royal finances

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a minister in Swift's satire.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who keeps a body's funds; Flimnap was Lord High keeper of Lilliput's purse.

clue.text: They support no end of tra. traditional-stories

indicators.note: no here says that the following word is to be dropped from the stories

parts.note: legends are old tales handed down
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that props up an endless supply of folk tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' tells you to take the letters END out of LEGENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs or table supports bear the weight of a body or a piece of furniture.

clue.text: This water tinged with pink was good for a Pobble's toes

definitions.text: This water tinged with pink was good for a Pobble's toes

parts.words: This water tinged with pink was good for a Pobble's toes
parts.note: in Edward Lear's poem The Pobble Who Has No Toes, Aunt Jobiska recommends a scented water tinged with pink

explanation.surface: A remedy for a nonsense creature's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender water, a scented toilet water named after the fragrant plant, which Lear's Aunt Jobiska prescribed.

clue.text: US football ground where we get a grilling?

definitions.meaning: an American football field, marked with parallel lines
a metal grid used over a fire for cooking, with a play on being questioned hard

explanation.surface: An American stadium where visitors are interrogated.
explanation.definitionFit: An American football field, and a barred cooking grate used for broiling.

clue.text: One sign of agreement makes more

definitions.text: One sign of agreement makes more

parts.words: One sign of agreement makes more
parts.note: a single vote of yes, multiplied, gives the votes in favour in a division

explanation.surface: Nodding along encourages others to agree too.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour of a motion, as counted in Parliament.

clue.text: Obvious Welsh description of a son

definitions.meaning: in Welsh names ap means 'son of', so a son is 'ap' his father or mother

explanation.surface: A plain Welsh account of someone's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh surnames once used ap, 'son of', as in Llewelyn ap Gruffydd, so a son is AP PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearly visible or evident, and split as Welsh ap plus a mother or father.

clue.text: Heavenly yet anaesthetic sort of ale

parts.note: ether was an early general anaesthetic

indicators.note: a sort of ale is a version of it, its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: Celestial yet knock-out kind of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' and 'anaesthetic' both point at ether, the upper air and the old knock-out gas; 'sort of' shuffles the beer into EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial or light and airy, belonging to the upper sky.

clue.text: Smiles offering 'the burglar his modus operandi ?

definitions.meaning: Samuel Smiles wrote a famous Victorian book on personal improvement
a thief simply helps himself to other people's goods

explanation.surface: A cheerful grin, as a burglar goes about his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smiles' is not a grin but Samuel Smiles, the Victorian author of a celebrated guide to improving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Smiles's book on self-improvement, and the thief's method of helping himself.

clue.text: As an official she takes on half the rabble!

indicators.note: she is followed by the next piece, which she takes on
half signals only the first part of the word for the mob

parts.note: riff-raff means the rabble, disreputable people

explanation.surface: A woman in authority takes on half the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes RIFF from RIFF-RAFF. 'As an official' defines the answer in its role.
explanation.definitionFit: A law officer, a county's chief officer of justice.

clue.text: They are currently in circulation

parts.note: currently reads as 'in a current', so things swirling round in moving water rather than money in use

explanation.surface: Banknotes or coins presently in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirlpools or swirls of water moving against the main flow.

clue.text: The padre, he's in another form

definitions.text: The padre, he's in another form

indicators.note: putting the words into another form means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chaplain who has been transformed into someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: 'in another form' rearranges PADRE HE'S, and the result means changed in form.
explanation.definitionFit: Remodelled or given a new outline, like the clergyman made over.

clue.text: A little Dickensian

parts.note: the title character of Dickens's novel known by the epithet Little

explanation.surface: Something slightly old-fashioned in the style of Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy, heroine of Dickens's novel Little Dorrit, is the 'little' Dickens character.

clue.text: Scandinavians seem worried in the clutch of 'their fate

indicators.note: being held in a grip puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a Norn is one of the Fates of Norse mythology, the Scandinavians' own fate

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters are disturbed and shaken up

explanation.surface: Vikings look anxious in the grip of destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norns were the three Fates of Norse myth; 'worried' gives SEME and 'in the clutch of' holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Men of ancient Norway and Scandinavia, the Vikings.

clue.text: Nothing to pay, so no tears

definitions.meaning: occupying property without being charged for it
free of rents, a rent being a tear or rip

explanation.surface: No charge, so nobody need cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing without a charge to the landlord, and read literally, without any rips.

clue.text: Noisy cause 'of brotherly strife in " Alice "

definitions.text: Noisy cause 'of brotherly strife in " Alice

parts.words: Noisy cause 'of brotherly strife in " Alice
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass the twins Tweedledum and Tweedledee agree to fight over a spoilt toy

explanation.surface: A loud row between siblings in a story about Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's noisy toy, the spoilt one Tweedledum accuses Tweedledee of breaking.
